shared_context.topic: difference between canker sore and herpes

snippets.output: The distinction between a canker sore and herpes can be challenging, but there are clinical features that can help differentiate between the two.
snippets.pattern_notes: Topic statement plus elaboration about differentiating features—properties enumerated about the comparison.

snippets.output: Prodromal symptoms are often reported by patients with herpes infections but not typically with canker sores.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel contrast on the same axis (prodromal symptoms) for two conditions.

snippets.output: Canker sores are typically smaller and more shallow, with a well-defined border, whereas herpes lesions can be larger and more diffuse, with a less distinct border.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated lesion properties (size, depth, border) compared between conditions.

snippets.output: These clinical features are not always reliable, and a definitive diagnosis often requires laboratory confirmation.
snippets.pattern_notes: Because clinical features are unreliable, lab confirmation is needed—causal/conditional chain.

snippets.output: Laboratory tests can help differentiate between the two; for example, a viral culture or PCR can confirm the presence of herpes simplex virus.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates lab test options (viral culture, PCR) as ways to differentiate.

snippets.output: Some patients may experience overlapping symptoms between canker sores and herpes, making it challenging to make a definitive diagnosis without further testing.
snippets.pattern_notes: Overlapping symptoms cause diagnostic difficulty—causal connection.

snippets.output: Canker sores typically heal within 7–14 days, whereas herpes infections can persist longer than canker sores.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel comparison of duration between canker sores and herpes.

snippets.output: Canker sores are limited to the oral mucosa.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single-atom distinct fact about canker sore location, same topic as neighbors.

snippets.output: Herpes infections are associated with viral shedding.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single-atom distinct fact about herpes viral shedding, same topic as neighbors.

snippets.output: Canker sores are more common than herpes infections.
snippets.pattern_notes: Topic shifts to prevalence, a different dimension from surrounding clinical-feature comparisons.

snippets.output: Canker sores usually present as a single lesion within the oral cavity, whereas herpes infections often present with multiple lesions.
snippets.notes: #4–#5 are on the same comparison axis, namely lesion number/presentation, whereas #3 is about prevalence, so it introduces a different dimension.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel comparison on the lesion number axis; notes confirm same comparison dimension.

snippets.output: People with canker sores often report a history of recurring lesions, while people with herpes infections may report a history of multiple episodes of oral herpes.
snippets.notes: #10–#11 form a coherent snippet because both concern recurrence history relevant to distinguishing recurrent canker sores from recurrent oral herpes
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel patient-history features (recurrence) compared between the two conditions.

snippets.output: Patients with herpes infections may report a history of multiple episodes of genital herpes.
snippets.notes: #12 is less directly aligned with the oral comparison, since a history of genital herpes is only indirectly informative, so it is better kept separate.
